text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Police commander Reijo Naulapaa says police need up to 100 million markka in extra financing next autumn; finance ministry has set up a committee to study the police's use of funds.
- Snowfall and freezing night temperatures will continue until next week, meteorologists say.
- State subsidies have encouraged companies and local governments to restructure production into flexible teams and cellular production units. @

- Leftist Alliance chairman Claes Andersson expects a majority of party members to oppose EMU in a poll next autumn but says this would not mean the party has to leave government. Members will also vote on participation in government.
- Cooperative-based dairy goods group Valio may lose two important dairies in western Finland due to disargument about prices.
- The Economist's Big Mac index shows markka is over 60 percent overvalued compared to the dollar. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- Construction growth may reach double digits this year if economy grows four to five percent, industry says.
- Merita to shut former KOP's main branch on Aleksanterinkatu and open a shopping centre instead.
- Analyst says corporate environmental reports have become an important tool for investment analysis.
AAMULEHTI
- European court will determine fate of Finland's alcohol monopoly Alko and state gambling monopoly RAY. @
- Tampere-based neon signs maker Tammerneon is planning to build factories in Hungary and Poland but this would not take jobs from Tampere, managing director says.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finnish constitution does not require a referendum on EMU but parliament may demand to hear the people's voice, says military academy strategy department reseacher Teija Tiilikainen.
- Transition to euro requires a constitutional change, says Supreme Administratrative Court president Pekka Hallberg. @
- Twenty-four percent of Finns are satisfied with Paavo Lipponen's goverment which just marked its first two years, in poll by Suomen Gallup.
- Department store Stockmann has gained a firm foothold on the Tallinn market in competition against Estonian Kaubamaja, says Stockmann's local head.
